articles.title_orig: China import expo spotlights deeper Asia-Pacific industrial cooperation
articles.title_zh: China import expo spotlights deeper Asia-Pacific industrial cooperation
articles.content_orig:
From New Zealand alpaca fiber processed in China to Thai beverages tailored for Chinese consumers, businesses across the Asia-Pacific are forging closer industrial ties at the ongoing China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, extending cooperation beyond trade in goods to encompass manufacturing, innovation and supply chains.
The ninth edition of the expo comes as China prepares to host the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen later this month, with openness, innovation and cooperation identified as the three priority areas for this year’s APEC cooperation.
Strong participation by businesses from APEC economies underscores the appeal of China’s vast market. Canadian and New Zealand exhibitors occupied their largest exhibition areas in the CIIE’s history this year. Australian companies expanded their exhibition space by 25 percent from last year. Meanwhile, U.S. exhibitors retained the largest exhibition area for the eighth consecutive edition.
Since its launch in 2018, the CIIE has evolved into a major platform for international trade and investment, with cumulative intended deals exceeding 580 billion U.S. dollars over its first eight editions and more than 3,400 new products, technologies and services making their debuts.
For New Zealand-based Pacific Alpacas, the journey from a small exhibition booth to a cross-border supply chain illustrates how market access can lead to deeper industrial collaboration.
After selling out its alpaca quilts during its CIIE debut in 2021, the company shipped 3.3 tonnes of alpaca fiber to China for processing in 2022, tapping into Chinese manufacturing expertise before establishing long-term partnerships with Chinese e-commerce platforms in 2025.
Through the expo, the company also forged partnerships with a textile mill in east China’s Jiangsu Province that helped improve the quality of its quilts, and a marketing agency in Shandong Province that helped it expand into livestream commerce.
“What matters more is the spillover effect,” Hu Tao, director of Pacific Alpacas, told Xinhua, referring to the business opportunities generated beyond the six-day expo.
Beyond traditional merchandise trade, multinational companies are increasingly integrating China’s manufacturing strengths and innovation capabilities into their regional and global operations.
Japanese electronics giant Panasonic, a nine-time CIIE participant, is advancing its strategy from “China for China” to “China for Global,” leveraging a network of more than 3,000 suppliers in China to strengthen its research, development and supply chain capabilities.
“We roll out innovative products and supply chain capabilities developed in China worldwide,” said Masaharu Nakayama, an executive officer of Panasonic Holdings Corporation, describing the company’s “Innovate in China, Deploy Globally” model.
For Thailand’s TCP Group, the company behind the Red Bull brand, regional cooperation is also taking shape through localized product innovation and long-term manufacturing investment.
Its new vitamin electrolyte beverage for Chinese consumers draws on a product concept developed in Thailand, with flavors tailored to local preferences and the product developed and manufactured by its China-based teams in collaboration with local supply chain partners.
The company’s production bases in China’s Sichuan Province and Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region have further deepened its integration into China’s industrial and supply chains, while the CIIE provides opportunities to gauge market response to new products and connect with business partners, according to the company.
Greater connectivity is also opening doors for smaller businesses, including Malaysian agricultural producers showcasing tropical fruits such as Musang King and Black Thorn durians at the expo to connect with Chinese buyers.
In 2025, APEC’s 21 member economies were home to 3 billion people and accounted for 61.6 percent of global real GDP, according to official APEC statistics.
Ng Yih Pyng, president of the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia, said he expects the upcoming APEC CEO Summit to help promote smoother trade and economic flows, deeper industrial cooperation and more tangible business opportunities for companies across the region.
For Thai businesses, the CIIE offers a gateway to the Chinese market, helping smaller firms find customers and test business models while enabling larger companies to deepen cooperation, said Paijit Viboontanasarn, vice chairman and secretary general of the Thai Chamber of Commerce in China.
“There are many forms of cooperation. It is not just about finding importers,” he said, adding that the expo helps companies build brands, connect with online and offline sales channels, and explore different partnerships.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces bipartisan congressional scrutiny over reported China spy link
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces bipartisan congressional scrutiny over reported China spy link
articles.content_orig:
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Some are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about the matter.
"The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I'm convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn't corrupt," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. "Congress will investigate and get answers."
Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January.
Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday requesting that he sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People's Republic of China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang .
The reports refer to Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions.
Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, The New York Times first reported on Friday.
When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times.
Rizzo said the Nvidia CEO's interactions with Ms. Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia's customers, the Times reported .
Separately, Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn shared a Times article published Saturday reporting that the Trump administration approved a Chinese firm, New Matrix, to assemble chips for Nvidia in Beijing. The Times found little evidence of meaningful operations at its listed address, despite Trump's Commerce Department clearing it for national security risks.
Cornyn called the report "outrageous" in his post on X .
Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., who sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security, called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify before Congress along with Huang.
Neither Nvidia nor the Commerce Department immediately responded to CNBC's request for comment.

articles.title_orig: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.title_zh: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump told reporters Friday that the U.S. carried out "minor strikes" on Iran, amid reports that two missiles struck Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz.
The missiles struck the island on Friday, Iranian news agency Tasnim reported, according to Reuters . Tasnim said there was no official information on damage, Reuters added.
The island lies off Iran's southern coast, near the Strait of Hormuz, the vital artery for oil and gas that has become a flashpoint in the war.
Speaking to reporters Friday evening after landing in West Palm Beach, Florida, Trump didn't comment specifically on Qeshm Island, saying: "I don't want to talk about it."
But he added: "We do minor strikes, but they knock out. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five." He did not explicitly confirm that he was referring to the reported strikes on Qeshm.
The strikes are the first since Tuesday's midterm elections, after analysts and regional officials had debated whether the vote would lead Trump toward further escalation or renewed diplomacy.
The U.S. struck the same island Monday, in what a U.S. official told MS Now was a " defensive measure ."
Trump also told reporters Friday that Iran wants "to make a deal very badly. They have 300% inflation. Their navy's gone. Their airport, everything's gone, and they want to make a deal."
The International Monetary Fund forecast that Iran's consumer prices would rise by an average of 78.6% in 2026, in a report published Oct. 13.
When asked if he wanted to make a deal "really soon," Trump said: "Well, we have nobody getting hurt, nobody getting killed.
"You know, this is a war that we may have been there for seven months, but we probably fought for three or four weeks, really fought. And again, you look at World War One; that's a war. World War Two; that's a war."
Iran has said it wants more than "paper commitments" from the U.S. before entering a new phase of diplomatic talks.
"We must see practical measures by the Americans," Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state broadcaster IRIB on Friday, according to Press TV .

articles.title_zh: At least four killed and dozens injured in train collision near Giza in Egypt, health ministry says
articles.content_orig:
Children were among the injured people seen being carried into a nearby hospital
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia.
There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.
Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.
The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.
Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured.
The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.
The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.
A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there.
The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.
Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.
On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.
The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.
Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.
The Saudi Ministry of Energy later said the Aramco tower had been hit by falling shrapnel in what it said was an attempted attack.
The state-owned oil company's building suffered minor damage.
A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

articles.title_orig: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.title_zh: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.content_orig:
South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) party faces a major setback after last week’s municipal elections, leaving it in a weak position in coalition talks to form city governments.
With all votes counted on Sunday, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s ANC had just over 30 percent nationally against about 25 percent for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA).
That represents a drop of roughly 14 percentage points from its 2021 local elections performance.
Former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party won about 10 percent of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest of the ballots were split between hundreds of smaller parties.
While still the largest party in South Africa, the ANC’s support has steadily eroded as voters grow increasingly frustrated with corruption and the party’s failure to tackle unemployment, which tops 34 percent more than three decades after the end of apartheid.
Failures in basic services, such as water and electricity, have also contributed to the ANC’s vote share falling in local elections over the past 15 years.
The party failed to win an outright majority in any of the eight major metro areas, including Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Since no party won more than 50 percent of the votes in many cities, including South Africa’s commercial hub Johannesburg, the ANC and DA will have to team up or hash it out with smaller parties to form municipal governments.
Parties will have 14 days to negotiate before city councils are formed.
ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the result “catastrophic” for the ANC but said the party would not go begging for positions when coalition talks begin soon.
“When the people tell us we have fallen short, … the honest answer is not to argue with them but to go home and put our house in order,” Mbalula said on Saturday.
In Johannesburg, the DA led the count with about 35 percent of the votes, compared with 20 percent for the ANC.
That could give DA veteran Helen Zille, who campaigned on fixing potholes and leaking water pipes, a good chance of becoming mayor, depending on the coalition agreements reached.
The DA said in a statement that it would initiate coalition discussions with “political parties that share a commitment to clean and accountable government, rooting out corruption, service delivery for all, the rule of law, and non-racialism”.

articles.title_orig: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.title_zh: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.content_orig:
Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender
Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.
The raid took place before a court case in the The Hague this week which will decide whether the BYD has a case to answer over allegations that its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.
Motoring experts have likened BYD’s seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV to the Defender since it went on sale in China in September last year. The company is scheduled to launch the vehicle, which the BBC’s Top Gear magazine called the “Chinese Defender clone” , in the UK market in January at a price of £47,995, undercutting the Defender by more than £20,000.
BYD says on its website that “an unapologetically boxy profile delivers the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look”.
The price of JLR’s seven-seat Defender 110 starts from £68,465and is one of the country’s bestselling cars. The UK-based carmaker, which is owned by India’s Tata Motors, sold 29,500 Defenders to retail customers between July and September this year, compared with 25,370a year earlier.
The raid in the Netherlands was carried out by court-ordered bailiffs, with JLR suspecting that BYD reverse-engineered some of the technology that could be used in the Ti7, the Times reported. JLR wanted to secure the digital records before they could be destroyed.
JLR and BYD declined to comment on the “ongoing legal proceedings”.
The dispute with BYD is not the first legal case JLR has pursed against a Chinese company over copycat allegations. It won a legal case to stop Jiangling Motor Corporation selling a copycat vehicle in 2019 after a three-year court battle.
after newsletter promotion
In some cases JLR has taken a collaborative approach to dealing with the rise of China’s carmakers. It agreed to form a joint venture with Chery in a 2012 deal which later included licensing its discontinued Freelander brand with the company.
Chery’s Jaecoo model, which is not part of the joint venture, has been called the Temu Range Rover because of its similarities to the JLR vehicle after years of collaboration between the pair. It costs £10,000 less than JLR’s Range Rover.
The Jaecoo was the bestselling car in the UK in October, with 10,813 registrations, taking its market share from 2.07% to 4.30%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders. JLR’s sales of the Range Rover fell to 43,300 in the third quarter of this year, from 47,196 cars sold in the same months last year.

articles.title_orig: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
articles.title_zh: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
articles.content_orig:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo
Seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances.
Gamal said he saw about 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to hospital. He said some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and died.
Egypt’s president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, said in a social media post that he had ordered a prompt investigation.
Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian railway authority said.
Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district.
Egypt’s deadliest train crash was in 2002 when more than 300 people were killed after a fire broke out on an overnight train journeying from Cairo to southern Egypt.

articles.title_orig: UH restores patient access to MyChart system that was shut down by cybersecurity incident
articles.title_zh: UH restores patient access to MyChart system that was shut down by cybersecurity incident
articles.content_orig:
CLEVELAND —     Frustration is growing among some University Hospitals patients as a cybersecurity incident continues to disrupt the hospital system's network more than two weeks after it was first detected.
Patients say they are still dealing with limited access to online services, including MyChart, prescription information, test results and online bill pay.
With many digital services still unavailable, patients are being forced to handle routine healthcare needs over the phone.
Stephen Bloomfield, a lifelong UH patient, says the disruption has made it difficult to communicate with his doctors, manage prescriptions and access important medical information.
"I've never had anything that's gone on quite this long," Bloomfield said. "My bank, my Wi-Fi or email — none of this stuff ever lasts more than a few hours."
Bloomfield says he can no longer access visit notes from his doctor, renew prescriptions online or message physicians through MyChart. He also reports problems with claims processing and scheduling future appointments.
He says even getting someone on the phone has been challenging.
"It was a 20-minute wait on music waiting for them to actually answer the phones," Bloomfield said.
The disruption began October 22, when University Hospitals detected unusual activity on its servers. The health system disconnected its systems from the internet as a precaution while it investigated the incident.
More than two weeks later, some online services remain limited, with patients continuing to report problems accessing their medical information and managing appointments.
Bloomfield says he would like to see more frequent updates from the hospital system about when services might be restored.
"That's what I'd like to see — a little bit more honesty and timeliness with updates as to when this might actually end," he said.
In an updated statement dated November 5, University Hospitals said all of its hospitals; emergency departments and physician offices remain open and fully operational.
The health system says the vast majority of appointments and procedures are continuing. Patients who already have appointments should keep them and do not need to call to confirm.
However, patients who need to schedule appointments, make changes, check on prescriptions or pay bills will need to use alternative methods while online services remain disrupted.
UH says patients will be able to resume paying bills through MyChart once the system is restored.
The hospital system is also warning patients to be alert for scams during the disruption.
UH says it will never call, text or email patients asking for sensitive personal information, including passwords or full Social Security numbers.
Anyone who receives a suspicious call or message should not respond and should instead contact their doctor's office directly.
UH acknowledged that its call centers are experiencing unusually high call volumes and says it is working to increase capacity to handle incoming calls.
For now, patients are being asked to rely on phone calls for many services that were previously available online.
University Hospitals has not provided a specific timeline for when all affected digital services, including MyChart, will be fully restored.
Here is UH's full updated statement:
All UH hospitals, emergency departments and physician offices remain open and fully operational, and our caregivers continue to provide safe, high-quality care. We are experiencing unusually high call volumes in our call center and are working to increase our capabilities to manage incoming calls and continue the highest level of service to our patients.
University Hospitals will never call, text or email you to ask for personal information such as your password or your full Social Security number. If you receive a call or message that seems suspicious, do not respond. Hang up and call your doctor's office.
News 5 promises to Follow-Through and bring you the latest.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo heads to Milei's Argentina as tensions loom over austerity, Iran
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo heads to Milei's Argentina as tensions loom over austerity, Iran
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV plays with a child as he arrived at the square outside the Cathedral Basilica of Florida, Uruguay, the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three, to preside over Mass on the third day of his twelve-day apostolic journey to South America, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Andrew Medichini/AP hide caption
FLORIDA, Uruguay — Pope Leo XIV wrapped up his visit to Uruguay on Sunday by praising the women who have passed the Catholic faith onto younger generations, as he highlighted the role the church has played since the founding of Latin America's most secular country.
Leo traveled to the city of Florida, north of Montevideo, to mark an important Catholic feast day before heading to Argentina for the second leg of his South American tour. It's expected to be the most politically delicate stop, given the Catholic Church's sharp criticisms of the austerity program of libertarian President Javier Milei.
For his final event in Uruguay, Leo celebrated the feast of the Virgin of the Thirty-three. According to tradition, 33 independence patriots acquired the Guaraní statue and had it with them when independence was declared from the Brazilian empire in Florida on Aug. 25, 1825.
Leo became the first pope in nearly four decades to visit Uruguay, in hopes of reminding its people that the Catholic Church is part of their very identity as a nation — even if, in subsequent decades, the country went on a deeply secular, and at times anticlerical, route.
In his homily, delivered in front of Florida's cathedral, Leo recalled the presence of the statue at the time of independence in reminding Uruguayans that "the history of peoples, too, cannot be fully understood without reference to God," and especially a mother.
He thanked all the mothers and grandmothers who have passed the faith onto younger generations, and acknowledged their pain when their efforts didn't stick.
"You taught your children to pray, and today they no longer do so. You used to attend Mass together, and it has been years since they entered a church," he said. But he urged them to not despair.
"Mothers and grandmothers: never tire of passing on the faith!"
Tens of thousands of people packed Florida's main square for the Mass under brilliant blue skies, some walking for several kilometers (miles) to reach the site. The city has a population of about 40,000 but the Vatican estimated 50,000 were on hand.
Fiama Pirez, an English professor, traveled from Montevideo for the Mass even though she could have seen Leo in the capital. She said she preferred a family outing to Florida so her mother could fulfill a dream to see a pope.
"I'm religious in my own way, and although I never strayed far from the Catholic faith, I'm rediscovering it today," she said.
Pope Leo XIV is cheered by faithful as he arrives for a prayer vigil at Centenario Stadium in Montevideo, on the second day of his twelve-day apostolic journey to South America, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Andrew Medichini/AP hide caption
In Buenos Aires, Milei is due to greet Leo at the airport before the two appear together for the traditional welcome ceremony and exchange of speeches. The Catholic Church has criticized Milei's austerity measures that have slashed social spending, and his embrace of artificial intelligence.
Milei has staked his presidency on cutting social spending to overhaul Argentina's troubled economy and deliver a long-elusive budget surplus. He has called social justice "an aberration" that amounts to stealing, and mocked as "huge stupidity" the increasingly common complaint in Argentina that families squeezed by his austerity program can't make it to the end of the month.
Leo, who took his name from the 19th-century pope whose encyclical on labor laid the foundation of Catholic social teaching, has made the poor and vulnerable a focus of his papacy, carrying on the legacy of his Argentine predecessor, Pope Francis.
Posters reading "At last, a Lion who unites" appeared across Buenos Aires this weekend, a jab playing on the pope's name in Spanish — León, or lion — and the lion imagery Milei often uses to portray himself on social media.
"Argentina is a society currently experiencing significant upheaval, deep polarization, and an economic crisis, along with a president who defies conventional protocol — a leader who, at one point, even challenged Pope Francis," said Luis Bahamondes, a professor at the Center for Judaic Studies at the University of Chile.
Since taking office in December 2023, Milei has slashed Argentina's healthcare budget by 48% in real terms. Planned cuts to the public university system, which represents a near-universal point of pride in the crisis-prone country, sent students into the streets.
According to official data, poverty in Argentina reached 32.3% of the population during the first half of 2026, representing about 15 million people.
Much like its allies in the Trump administration, Milei's government has portrayed the cuts as part of a necessary reform process to remake Argentina's troubled economy and eliminate fraud and waste in the federal bureaucracy.
Like Trump, Milei has also courted AI investment and data centers with promises of limited regulation. Leo has warned that the AI race poses threats to humanity and the environment and called for strict, internationally policed safeguards on its development.
Milei's government insists the papal trip is purely religious. "The pope belongs to all Argentines. He doesn't belong to a political party or a political camp," Karina Milei, the president's sister and secretary-general of the presidency, told reporters after a recent planning meeting for Leo's visit with church leaders.
In Argentina, Leo is completing unfinished business left by Francis. The Argentine Jesuit, the former archbishop of Buenos Aires, never returned home during his 12-year pontificate, confounding friends and foes alike.
"There's a lot of disagreement over Francis and his legacy in Argentina," said David Lantigua, a theology professor and faculty fellow at the University of Notre Dame's Kellogg Institute, which focuses especially on Latin American affairs.
Much of the polemics stems from his tenure in Buenos Aires, when the former Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio was a slum priest who advocated for the poorest and most marginalized — the sector of Argentines feeling Milei's social spending cuts the most.
"I think we'll see that kind of tension with Leo — that's the ministry Francis left behind," Lantigua said.
Leo, who spent two decades as a missionary priest in Peru ministering to poor people, is very much a pastor in Francis' image and owes his pontificate to the late pope. But unlike Francis, he is returning home to Peru on the last leg of this trip, visiting a country where he spent two decades as a missionary.
Argentina's state intelligence agency said Saturday that a person had been arrested over death threats against Leo ahead of his arrival. A federal court in Campana, some 70 kilometers (45 miles) northwest of Buenos Aires, ordered the arrest less than 24 hours after the agency was tipped off, it said, without elaborating.

articles.title_orig: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Milei’s Argentina
articles.title_zh: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Milei’s Argentina
articles.content_orig:
By Deborah Castellano Lubov
"May Christ truly enter into what you do, what you love, what you choose â even those aspects of your life that no one sees. Be saints! Do not settle for a merely decent life or for a habitual faith, content with doing only the essential. Do not give God only a part of yourselves â give yourselves completely!"
Pope Leo XIV offered this encouragement during a prayer vigil in Montevideo held on Saturday evening, on the second day of his Apostolic Journey to Uruguay.
READ POPE LEO'S FULL REMARKS
In his remarks, the Holy Father called on the faithful to live a life of holiness, explaining that doing so fills our hearts and satisfies our deepest longings.
Explaining that saints are men and women who overflow with the abundance of life in Christ, Pope Leo stressed that they are free and authentic people whose lives make it attractive to say a resounding "yes" to love, truth, and happiness.
"Do not be afraid, then, to aspire to holiness," Pope Leo said, stressing that "Christ did not call us to mediocrity; He called us to a new and full life like His own."
Reflecting on growing secularization and increasingly widespread religious indifference experienced by many Christian communities today, he acknowledged the challenges facing the Church.
The Pope commended those who, even in these circumstances, continue to persevere in their faith, recalling "parents who pray with their children, teachers who strive to live and bear witness to their faith, and young people who have discovered Christ and wish to follow Him even when they feel alone."
The Pope also remembered communities that continue to gather, and priests who travel great distances to bring the sacraments to the faithful.
Pope Leo warned that "when we try to build a world without God, we run the risk of leaving humanity without a place as well." Yet, he insisted, none of this changes the reality that "that Child is God, and He comes to save us."
Pope Leo emphasized that this "us" includes each and every one of us, noting that indifference can also creep, little by little, into the lives of those who believe.
The Pope called on the faithful to ask themselves whether they truly make enough room for Christ in their lives.
"Is there room in our time, in our way of thinking, in our homes? Is there room to listen to him, to receive his forgiveness, to allow his word to correct us? We need to keep Christ at the center of our lives through prayer, Mass, Confession and the meditative reading of the Gospel," Pope Leo urged.
"We must all become disciples again and again. If we want others to find Christ," he stressed, "we need to know the way to Bethlehem ourselves first."
Pope Leo then invited all the faithful to reflect with humility and simplicity on the light of Christ in their own lives.
"Perhaps there are people who would never open a Bible on their own, who have not set foot in a church in years, or who cannot even say whether they believe in God. But when they see you, the desire for God may be awakened in them; they may even discover that it is worth risking their lives to find Him," the Pope said.
The Pope called on the faithful to embrace courage and faith when making the major decisions of life.
"Young people, dare to take the step of marrying and starting a family yourselves. Do not be afraid of 'forever'!" Pope Leo encouraged.
"Married couples, open your home to life, even when the world tells you that a child is a burden," the Holy Father continued.
Pope Leo also urged those who feel called to the priesthood or consecrated life not to let fear prevent them from responding to God's invitation.
"If any of you feel that Christ is calling you to leave everything behind to follow Him in the priesthood or in consecrated life, do not ignore that voice out of fear of missing out on other opportunities," he said.
Moreover, the Pope added, "When being just and honest comes at a price, pay it. When forgiving seems like a defeat, forgive. When everyone tells you to think of yourselves first, do not be afraid to put yourselves in the last place," and "give up time, money, comfort and plans to serve others."
"May those who see you," Pope Leo said, find themselves asking: "Why do they live in this way? Where do they get this freedom? Why do they love one another so much?"
"If our lives spark a question," the Pope noted, "they will have borne fruit when that question guides someone to Jesus. To shed much light, we do not need to be many, but rather to reflect the Lord's light."
"Good News needs witnesses, for we have received news that deserves to be proclaimed to the world: Jesus Christ!"
He stressed that we accordingly are called to proclaim God is with us and that through Jesus Christ, our sins can be forgiven.
The Holy Father continued by noting that, while society may find many valuable things in other institutions, none can replace the proclamation that God's love is stronger than death, hatred, violence, war, and sin.
"This," he affirmed, "is the joy we bring."
Pope Leo said he had come to visit the faithful of Uruguay to remind them of the joy found in Christ.
"May this encounter be like a visit to Bethlehem, so that you can return to your lives in a new way!" he encouraged.
"May it be evident that Christ lives and that encountering him makes all the difference," the Pope urged. retierating, "That same Jesus who was born in Bethlehem, who died and rose again, lives forever and remains with us," "awaiting us," "truly present in the Eucharist."
Stressing that "we can continue to encounter Him â so near and so humble â in every tabernacle," Pope Leo exhorted, "Seek Him there, in Eucharistic adoration."
The Holy Father called on the faithful to cultivate constant closeness with Christ.
"Speak to Him, as you would to a friend," he suggested, saying, "let Him look upon you."
Finally, Pope Leo invited those gathered to join him in placing their lives under the gaze of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three, saying, "May she, the Morning Star who leads us to her Son, teach us to recognize him and follow him."
The Pope concluded by inviting everyone to ask the Lord for the grace to respond faithfully to His call, just as Mary did: "Here I am, Lord; here is your servant. Let your will be done in me!"

articles.title_orig: Apple Taking New Approach to Developing iOS 28 and macOS 28
articles.title_zh: Apple Taking New Approach to Developing iOS 28 and macOS 28
articles.content_orig:
Apple has made a change to its development process for iOS 28, macOS 28, and corresponding software updates, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman.
In his Power On newsletter today , he said Apple separates development of each year's new operating systems into three major stages. Typically, he said each stage consists of four weeks of coding followed by a four-week "convergence" period where new features are integrated into the operating systems. This time around, Apple has made a change.
The first stage of development for iOS 28 and the other updates apparently consisted of six weeks of coding and two weeks of feature convergence. This change gives Apple's software engineers more time to come up with new features.
"Instead of the normal split between two four-week efforts, Apple engineers were tasked with six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development, and then only two weeks of convergence," he said. "Employees say they like the change, indicating that it creates more time for coming up with ideas and exploring them before needing to lock things in."
Gurman did not reveal any specific features planned for iOS 28. The update should be available in beta in June and released in September next year.

articles.title_orig: Vinted and eBay could be included in under-16 social media ban, minister says
articles.title_zh: Vinted and eBay could be included in under-16 social media ban, minister says
articles.content_orig:
Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.
Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".
The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.
Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."
It came after the Sunday Times reported that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.
The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.
Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".
Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.
The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.
A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".
"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.
An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".
"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.
The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms.
YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures.
A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material".
That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites.
It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s. However, certain features such as its chat function will be restricted.
But Matthew Sinclair, a senior director at the Computer and Communications Industry Association, which represents tech companies, argued that ministers should prevent the rules having "scope creep".
He said a restriction on messaging for under-16s "would not stop at social media and would reach into the services families depend on to stay in touch", and urged the government to "ensure any new restrictions are proportionate and effective."
The UK's ban comes after a similar one was introduced in Australia last year.
Many children there have found ways to get round it, but the UK has said it intends to take a tougher approach.
In recent weeks, attention has turned to how a social media ban would be enforced.
Last month, the communications regulator Ofcom set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.
Rani Govender, head of online child safety at the NSPCC, said the "real question" going forward was how the government ensured age checks were effective.
"But effective age checks are only part of the solution," she added. "Tech companies must also be required to build child safety into every platform, device and AI tool, so children are protected from harmful and illegal content and only able to access age-appropriate services."

articles.title_orig: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 100 others, authorities said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry. One of the trains derailed, it said, but did not specify which.
The Health Ministry said at least four people were killed and 88 others were wounded. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, it said.
A train driver was among those killed in the collision, the Health Ministry said.
President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said in a social media post he is following the aftermath of the train collision "with great concern and extend my deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives."
"I have directed state agencies to provide the necessary medical care, promptly investigate the circumstances of the accident and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent," he wrote.
Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian Railway Authority said.
Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district.
Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

articles.content_orig:
crim has released El Shaddai: Zero Nine Reversi , “a board game that puts a bold twist on classic Reversi,” for PC via Steam at a 10 percent-off launch discount price of $3.59. The price will change to $3.99 after November 15.
El Shaddai: Zero Nine Reversi first launched for iOS via App Store and Android via Google Play on April 27. The mobile versions were updated alongside the PC release today with online multiplayer support and an archive.
Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page :
Zero Nine Reversi is a board game that puts a bold twist on classic Reversi. Every stone has HP.
The game includes two ways to play: “Classic,” a deep single-player challenge, and “Online,” where you pick a character and battle other players.
In normal Reversi, flipping a stone is the end of the story. In Zero Nine Reversi , a flipped stone loses 1 HP. When its HP reaches zero, the stone is purified and vanishes from the board. This simple change turns every match into a battle of attrition, where positioning, timing, and resource management matter as much as territory.
A versus mode where you choose a character and fight. On top of stone HP, it adds the “BUMP & BURST” rules and a unique ability for each character.

articles.title_orig: Apple CEO Presses Software Chief to Pursue More Ambitious AI Strategy
articles.title_zh: Apple CEO Presses Software Chief to Pursue More Ambitious AI Strategy
articles.content_orig:
In the past few years, a major Apple story (especially in the age of AI) has been that the company isn’t moving fast enough in the space to keep up with competitors. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman , new Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly pushing on software chief Craig Federighi to ‘accelerate’ Apple’s roadmap for software.
At the moment, there’s no indication that Apple’s well known software SVP Craig Federighi will be leaving the company. In fact, Craig has made it a very low priority of his to develop a succession plan in any sense, per Mark Gurman . That said, Ternus still wants to see change in how Craig Federighi thinks about Apple’s software strategy:
In recent weeks, Ternus held a closed-door meeting with Craig Federighi, who became Apple’s AI czar following last year’s dismissal of its former AI leader. Desiring more and frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors, Ternus pushed his software chief to accelerate the company’s road map and move quickly beyond merely making necessary improvements to Siri.
A large part of Federighi’s approach has been how hands-on he is, resulting in his viewpoint shaping how Apple’s software development goes to a large extent. That’s left team members feeling that they have ‘limited influence’ over what happens:
Federighi is known for taking an especially hands-on role in meetings and major decisions, with some employees describing a management style that can leave little room for competing ideas to gain traction. He is also known for vigorously debating opposing viewpoints, using his command of technical details and ability to argue his position to push back against proposals he disagrees with. That approach has at times frustrated members of the software engineering and design teams, some of whom believe they have limited influence over the direction of products.
Another part is that Federighi reportedly only plans for a 12-18 month timeframe, versus the years-long roadmaps used in hardware engineering. These are some of the gaps that Apple may want to bridge in the coming years.
Separately, Vision Pro and Siri AI leader Mike Rockwell is still seriously considering stepping down. He’s currently vice president of Siri engineering:
The management concerns go beyond Federighi. Mike Rockwell, who created the Vision Pro headset in addition to leading the development of Siri AI, continues to seriously consider stepping down. That could mean leaving his role as vice president of Siri engineering — or Apple altogether — next year. Such a move would be a major blow, given his role in bringing the new Siri to market after an embarrassing two-year delay.
In the same report, Gurman also reported that Apple is experimenting with a new development pipeline, giving engineers 50% more time to code and explore more, and spend less time on integration, as coding agents have improved.
It remains to be seen what else might change at Apple to enable faster development timelines, though it seems likely that Craig Federighi may have to release his ‘firm grip’ on the software engineering org, and instead allow some other leaders to blossom and act on their own accord.

articles.content_orig:
Players can collect and use an ephemeral new launch-celebration toy to enhance their campfire and spread the benefits of camaraderie as they begin their journey through Azeroth in World of Warcraft: Forever.
Watch any eligible World of Warcraft stream on Twitch.tv from November 4 at 4:30 pm PST to November 12 at 4:30 pm PST to claim the Pouch of Violet Dust Toy. This ephemeral item is available only within WoW: Forever and can only be used during the “WoW: Forever Launch Celebration” event period, which expires in early December. After that point, the toy will be removed from players’ collections and will no longer be available in game.
The Pouch of Violet Dust toy allows players to turn a campfire purple, increasing the duration of all camp benefits by 1 hour (for a total of a 2-hour duration). Once activated, this benefit is shared, and any other players resting at the Camp will receive the same duration extension.
To participate, you must link your Twitch account by visiting https://account.battle.net/connections . If you have changed your password or made any changes to your Twitch or Battle.net account, you will have to relink your accounts. When you relink, there will be a 7-day cooldown before you can relink a new Twitch account. After you’ve claimed your rewards on Twitch, please make sure you’re logging into the Battle.net region you’d like to receive the drop(s) on, as the first region you log into will be where your items will be delivered. It can take up to 24 hours to receive your reward(s) in-game after claiming. Read our Frequently Asked Questions section for more information.
Start Time: November 4, at 4:30 pm PST End Time: November 12, at 4:30 pm PST Where to Watch: Eligible World of Warcraft streams.
Watch four hours of eligible World of Warcraft content while Drops are active on any channel.
Q. How do I link my battle.net and Twitch accounts? A. Sign into your Battle.net account at https://account.battle.net/connections and click the Connect link for Twitch, then follow the instructions to sign in and link your Twitch account to Battle.net.
Q. How do I link my Battle.net account to my YouTube account? A. You can link your Battle.net account to your YouTube account through the YouTube Connected Apps page to earn game rewards and drops.
Q. What devices can I use to earn and claim drops? A. You can earn and claim drops using your PC/Mac web browser or on the Twitch or YouTube app for Android or iOS. Twitch apps or YouTube apps on game consoles, smart TVs, and other TV apps do not support drops.
Q. Do I need to watch the same channel the entire time to earn my drops? A. You can earn progress towards a drop on any eligible channel in the World of Warcraft category on Twitch. You can, for example, watch half an hour on one channel and then switch to another channel without losing your progress. You cannot earn progress faster by watching more than one channel at a time. If watching on YouTube, you’ll need to watch the World of Warcraft official channel for the entirety.
Q. Will I receive my drop rewards in-game automatically? A. To receive your rewards, you must claim the drop on the channel you’re watching or in the Drops Inventory menu on Twitch. YouTube rewards will be delivered automatically in-game if the Battle.net and YouTube accounts are connected while viewing.
Q. Do Twitch Drop rewards expire? A. Earned Twitch Drop rewards will expire seven (7) days after they’ve been claimed if a Battle.net account has not been linked.
Q. As a streamer, how do I get Twitch Drops on my channel? A. All you need to do is ensure your Twitch and Battle.net accounts are linked and that you’ve opted into Drops (see Drops Streamer Home).
Q. What regions are eligible for these Twitch Drops? A. Participating regions include North America, Latin America, Europe, The Middle East, Africa, Japan, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand.
Q. What regions are eligible for these YouTube Rewards? A. Participating regions include North America, Latin America, Europe, The Middle East, Africa, Japan, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, Korea, Australia, and New Zealand.

articles.title_zh: A ‘Chaotic Race’ for the World’s Top Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica extended her lead in the race for United Nations secretary-general in yet another informal ballot held by the Security Council. The two new candidates that joined the contest recently struggled to get the minimum of nine “encourage” votes.
In the straw poll on Thursday, Nov. 5, Grynspan got 12 encourage ballots, one higher than the last straw poll, on Oct. 30, according to multiple leaked results seen by PassBlue. The number of “discourage” votes for her also dropped to three, but she needs to get zero discourage, including no veto, for the Council recommend her as the nominee to the General Assembly.
In Thursday’s undifferentiated straw poll, it is unclear which Council members cast a discourage vote against Grynspan, though there is plenty of speculation that it has consistently been the US throughout the series of informal balloting and possibly Russia this time — both veto holders. A color-coded ballot reveals vetos from a permanent member (Britain, China and France as well), but not who cast them.
No date has been set for another straw poll or whether it will be color-coded. (The only such poll in the race so far was held on Oct. 16.)
Lana Nusseibeh , a candidate from the United Arab Emirates (who was born in 1978), and Feridun Sinirlioglu , 70, of Türkiye, are the newest entrants in the race. From the start of her nomination, announced on Oct. 21, Nusseibeh has been facing strong pushback from civil society groups as the media also scrutinize her country’s enabling role in the war in Sudan and its related atrocities.
The New York Times reported on Nov. 5 that UN investigators had linked an Emirati security company to the country’s ruling family to deploy Colombian mercenaries alongside the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group fighting the Sudanese Armed Forces in Sudan’s civil war. Nusseibeh, who until recently was a top UAE diplomat, has over the years repeatedly denied Emirati support of the RSF.
Soon after she announced her candidacy as UN secretary-general, Human Rights Watch questioned whether she would defend the independence of UN investigative bodies examining her government’s actions in Sudan and elsewhere.
The UAE authorities also repeatedly reject allegations that they support either side in Sudan’s war, despite numerous UN independent inquiries and other expert institutions saying otherwise. That includes a Human Rights Council’s fact-finding mission report published in September, saying the UAE has “played a significant role in networks involved in the recruitment, financing, transportation and deployment” of foreign military contractors and the provision of military-related support benefiting the RSF.
Nusseibeh is saying in her campaign that ending the conflict will be a priority if she is selected UN chief. But human rights experts say that even if she commissioned an independent UN inquiry into the Sudan war, as the head of the UN, it could be challenging for her to separate such a step from her country’s own geopolitical ambitions.
Sinirlioglu announced his candidacy on Oct. 30. He is a former foreign minister, UN ambassador and currently the secretary-general of the Organization for the Security and Cooperation in Europe. In Thursday’s straw poll, he received three encourage, eight discourage and four “no opinion” votes, far below the threshold to be a viable contender. Like another candidate in the race, Olara Otunnu of Uganda, the Turk was included in the Council’s informal ballot before he met with the General Assembly, a formality in which the other nominees have participated.
The public dialogue for Sinirlioglu is scheduled for Nov. 6, and an informal, private meeting with Council members is planned for Nov. 9.
An outside expert on the UN race told PassBlue that China may be insisting for now that the informal polling remain undifferentiated rather than color-coded to give more time to candidates from the Latin American region — of which there are five — to drum up more support while Beijing continues to assess Nusseibeh.
In May, China’s representative at the UN told reporters that his country preferred that a woman — without specifying who — should clinch the top UN post and that the selection process should abide by the UN’s regional rotation system. (The UN has never been led by a woman, and the Latin American-Caribbean area says it’s their turn for the job.)
In Thursday’s poll, Rafael Grossi of Argentina remained second, with nine encourage, four discourage and two no opinions, reflecting no change from the Oct. 30 balloting. Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett of Guyana also retained her same spot from the last poll, with eight encourage, but her discourage numbers fell to five from six and she drew two no opinions, one more than last time.
Otunnu got four encourage, nine discourage and two no opinions. María Fernanda Espinosa, backed by Antigua and Barbuda but an Ecuadorian, received three encourage, 10 discourage and two no opinion. The results of the Tonga-nominated Ivonne A-Baki (also Ecuadorian) remained unchanged: One encourage and 14 discourage.
The second term of Secretary-General António Guterres ends on Dec. 31.
Damilola Banjo is an award-winning staff reporter for PassBlue who has covered a wide range of topics, from Africa-centered stories to gender equality to UN peacekeeping and US-UN relations. She also oversees all video production for PassBlue. She was a Dag Hammarskjold fellow in 2023 and a Pulitzer Center postgraduate fellow in 2021. She was part of the BBC Africa team that produced the Emmy-nominated documentary, "Sex for Grades." In addition, she worked for WFAE, an NPR affiliate in Charlotte, N.C. Banjo has a master's of science degree from the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism and an undergraduate degree from the University of Ibadan in Nigeria.
We would love your thoughts. Please comment:
The race for the next Secretary General is now a competition between candidates over who can be the most anodyne.  Venality and the collective abrogation of responsibility by the leaders of the P-5 and by the many and varied sheep in the General Assembly has brought us here.  Not even the stalwart supporters of the UN system have risen to its defence and insisted on better.  Not a peep from the Nordics.  Utter silence from Canada.  Acquiescence from South Africa.  The list goes on…
But it gets worse. Fully 7 members of the Security Council judge Ms. Nussebeih of the UAE to be a suitable candidate for UN Secretary General even though, on the evidence, she is just about the closest one can get in international relations to being an adjudicated liar.  Is this a firm foundation for the highest level of diplomacy?
These are shameful days for the purported stewards of the Westphalian state system.  Historians in every language will look back in amazement on these times.  And they will surely ask, “How could they have been so stupid?”.
Thank you again Damilola/Pass Blue. Easily the best reporting on the UNSG race.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.content_orig:
Former military chief says prime minister brought Israel to historic crisis and it is approaching ‘point of no return’
Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task of forming a government on Sunday, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he said the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.
Eisenkot, 66, the leader of the Yashar party, who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from the president, Isaac Herzog, who gave him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.
“We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the state of Israel,” said Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie at a ceremony at the presidential office. “We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps.”
Eisenkot faces significant challenges on the road to becoming prime minister. He has three options: a power-sharing agreement with Netanyahu, support from Arab-led parties – something several members of his bloc do not support – or an agreement with the ultra-Orthodox parties, which demand military exemptions for their community.
Eisenkot and Herzog acknowledged Israel’s growing isolation under Netanyahu, who is wanted by the international criminal court.
In the US, Israel’s closest ally, Democrats on Tuesday swept the midterm elections, with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war, which Netanyahu launched with Donald Trump.
Eisenkot said: “We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed.”
He appealed to Netanyahu’s Likud party as well as the far-right party of the finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, to join him – but only with himself as prime minister.
“My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment,” he said.
Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a coalition, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving premier.
Eisenkot’s wide-ranging opposition bloc won 48 of the Israeli parliament’s 120 seats in the October elections, while Netanyahu’s camp secured 53, leaving neither with a majority.
During party consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received the endorsements of both Arab-majority lists, who could now play kingmakers after making unprecedented gains in the vote.
Eisenkot has laid out a series of conditions for any Arab party to join his coalition, including recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and declaring the Palestinian militant group Hamas a terrorist organisation. One of his partners, the more conservative Yisrael Beiteinu party, has already said it will not join a coalition with Arab-led parties.
Eisenkot, a former army chief, and his partners made equal military service a central part of their campaign. Specifically, they are seeking an end to the longstanding draft exemptions enjoyed by the ultra-Orthodox.
Netanyahu has repeatedly claimed the election was “stolen” by Arab parties , which rallied their supporters to vote in large numbers. But he has offered little to no evidence to support the claims.
Netanyahu is expected to continue his pressure tactics against Eisenkot, saying any alliance with the Arab parties would be an act of betrayal.
Israel’s Shin Bet security agency has launched an investigation into possible foreign interference in the vote, but the country’s Central Elections Committee – and Herzog – say the vote was valid and even if wrongdoing was found, it did not have a significant impact on the result.
Netanyahu called for a “national unity” government with Eisenkot on Saturday night but it remains unclear whether the two rivals could agree on a power-sharing agreement. These types of coalition governments are notoriously fragile and often collapse.
Eisenkot, the military chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, has set out to unite Israelis after Netanyahu’s divisive tenure, under which the country moved sharply to the right.
He has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity, decrying recent incidents as “Jewish terror” abetted by Netanyahu’s government.
He opposes the creation of a Palestinian state and has vowed to end Hamas’s rule in Gaza and destroy the Islamist movement’s military wing.
Commanding the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah, Eisenkot devised the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”. The idea, named after a Beirut suburb heavily damaged in that war, involves Israel vowing to use massive force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by the Lebanese militant movement Hezbollah.
After his appointment, Eisenkot will have 28 days to come up with the 61 votes needed for a government. If he comes up short, Herzog can provide a 14-day extension before he has to offer the mandate to someone else.
If neither side succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections. The country held five elections between 2019 and 2022 owing to repeated deadlocks.

articles.title_orig: 2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland Gains An Inch Where It Counts, All PHEVs Get NACS And Level 3 Charging
articles.title_zh: 2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland Gains An Inch Where It Counts, All PHEVs Get NACS And Level 3 Charging
articles.content_orig:
The ever-popular Toyota RAV4 was totally redesigned for the 2026 model year, and for the first time ever it offered exclusively hybridized drivetrains . Considering how momentous that redesign was, one would expect second-year updates to be minimal, and that's mostly the case for the 2027 RAV4, but the handful of updates are good ones. The off-road-oriented RAV4 Woodland becomes slightly more off-road oriented for 2027 with a reworked suspension that adds an inch of ground clearance for a total of 9.1 inches, and all plug-in-hybrid RAV4s, including the RAV4 GR Sport , now feature an NACS port with DC fast-charging abilities and an 11-kW onboard AC charger.
I'm never happy to see prices increase, but at least Toyota has kept the increases to a minimum, with different trim levels costing between $400 and $755 more than they did last year . The cheapest 2027 Toyota RAV4 you can buy is the front-wheel-drive LE trim that now costs $33,895, up $400 from last year, while the cheapest 2027 RAV4 PHEV you can buy is the all-wheel-drive SE that now costs $43,695, which is $600 dearer than last year.
The RAV4 Woodland's new raised suspension includes new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers that accompany its added inch of clearance, and it also gets redesigned all-weather floor mats. That lift comes at a cost, with the 2027 Woodland being $755 more expensive at $42,250, and it gets 1 mpg worse in the city than last year — it's rated at a still outstanding 40 mpg city, 35 mpg highway, and 38 mpg combined, though. ( The Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid offers 0.2 inches more ground clearance than the Woodland's 9.1 inches, if that really matters to you.) The PHEV Woodland loses 3 miles of EV range, now standing at 46 miles, and though its city fuel economy dropped 3 mpg to 38, its highway mileage went up by 1 mpg to 35, and its combined rating remains 37 mpg.
The 2026 RAV4 GR Sport plug-in hybrid perplexed us because it had worse charging abilities than all other PHEV RAV4s, but that's amended for 2027. All plug-in RAV4s are now fitted with an NACS port for the first time, and the GR Sport gains DC fast-charging capability and the 11-kW onboard charger the rest of the lineup already had. Every PHEV RAV4 is now capable of charging from 10% to 80% in the same time as last year, about 35 minutes. For some reason, the 2027 RAV4 GR Sport's electric-only driving range drops by 3 miles to an estimated 45 miles of range, but that's still a good result.
Other tweaks include all the PHEVs now having their charge port on the driver's side, every model gains a standard backup camera washer, and all-wheel-drive RAV4s now have Multi-Terrain Select with Rock & Dirt mode and Mud & Sand mode. Toyota says 2027 RAV4 hybrids should hit dealer lots later this year, but PHEV models will arrive early next year.

articles.title_orig: Train collision in Egypt’s Giza province injures 64 as crews rush to clear wreckage
articles.title_zh: Train collision in Egypt’s Giza province injures 64 as crews rush to clear wreckage
articles.content_orig:
At least seven people were killed and 112 people injured after two trains collided in Egypt on Sunday, the country’s health ministry said.
Several carriages were derailed after one train collided with the rear of another between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza, near the capital Cairo, the Egyptian National Railways Authority said in a statement.
Dozens of ambulances were dispatched to transport the injured to nearby hospitals, while cranes were deployed to remove the wreckage after traffic on the railroad was disrupted, Egyptian authorities said.
Among the dozens injured in the collision, 45 people have been discharged from nearby hospitals after their condition improved, according to the health ministry.
The Egyptian railway system, the oldest in Africa and the Middle East, has a long history of deadly accidents.
In 2019, a train lost control while approaching Cairo’s main station in Ramses Square, igniting a fire that killed 25 people. Another accident in 2017 occurred on the way to Alexandria, when a train derailed and collided head-on with another train, killing more than 40 people.
Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered an investigation into the Giza collision on Sunday, according to statement on his official Facebook page. He also offered his “sincere condolences” to those killed.
This story has been updated.
CNN’s Sana Noor Haq contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Europe will be represented in Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine, French foreign minister says
articles.title_zh: Europe will be represented in Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine, French foreign minister says
articles.content_orig:
Paris and Europe will have a seat at the table in next week’s U.S.-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on Sunday.
France “will be around the table,” Barrot told French radio RTL . “The Europeans will be well represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these discussions. I cannot yet tell you who will represent France on this occasion, but it will certainly be there.”
U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff announced last Monday there would be trilateral talks between Washington, Kyiv and Moscow on Nov. 10–11, the first since a summit in February. But the extent to which Europe will take part in the talks remains unclear.
“In recent weeks, Europeans have made their voices heard, expressing to the American mediator that no discussion concerning the future of the continent can disregard our expectations and demands,” Barrot told RTL.
European Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said Friday the EU executive didn’t yet have details to share, but added that “it’s obviously up to the European Union to decide on matters which affect its security and on matters which are of its competence.”
The EU has scrambled to agree on who should represent it at the peace talks and who, if anyone, should be in contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni urged European Council President António Costa to settle the issue in a letter this week, prompting Costa to put it on the agenda of the Nov. 13 leaders’ summit. Meloni’s letter was partly prompted by a phone call Finland’s Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Jonas Gahr Støre made to Putin on Oct. 27, which took some European leaders by surprise.
Meanwhile, the European Commission hosted talks on Ukraine’s reconstruction on Wednesday, bringing together representatives from Ukraine, the U.S., U.K., Germany, France, NATO and the World Bank.
U.S. President Donald Trump spoke late Thursday of a “big, beautiful agreement,” after meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev, adding: “It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe.” The plan has brought anxiety among EU officials, who fear it risks sidelining the continent and emboldening Putin.
“We already have a European security architecture in place — NATO and European Union both have their respective roles,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Friday in response to the U.S. plan. “We must make sure Ukraine is integrated into this architecture. The problem remains that Russia keeps breaking the treaties that underpin it … Putin does not have a veto over European security.”
